--------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 1 ‑ IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Main design: Regression-Discontinuity-in-Time Event Study (“RD-IV”)

Step 1 (RDD / first stage).  
• Exploit the sharp discontinuity at the bond-approval threshold (2/3 before Nov-2000, 55 % thereafter).  
• Running variable r ≡ VoteShare – Threshold.  
• Passage dummy Bᵈ = 1{r ≥ 0}.  
Because some narrowly-approved bonds are not fully issued (and some failing bonds are later re-introduced), the design is fuzzy; we treat Bᵈ as an instrument for realised facility spending.

Step 2 (Local IV / second stage).  
• Using only elections within a symmetric bandwidth h around r = 0 we estimate:  

 CapitalSpendingᵢₜ = α₀ + α₁ Bᵈᵢₜ + f(rᵢₜ) + Xᵢₜ′β + μ_district + γ_year + εᵢₜ  
 (Passage → $ of spending per pupil)  

• 2SLS: outcome Y (log house price, test score) on predicted capital spending, again within h.  

Step 3 (dynamic effects).  
• Event-time dummies k = −5 … +10 interacted with Bᵈ identify pre-trends and persistence.  
• District and calendar-year fixed effects difference-out time-invariant heterogeneity.  

Rationale  
(a) Institutional: voters can pass only a facilities bond via referendum, not by simple board vote. (b) Very many elections cluster tightly around the threshold → power. (c) Bonds are legally earmarked; current spending is not affected → cleaner channel.



--------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 2 ‑ TREATMENT AND CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Tᵢₜ = post-passage real capital expenditure per pupil financed by the focal bond (or a dummy =1 in all post-election years if looking at intent-to-treat).

Control group  
District-years in which the same bond proposal failed by a narrow margin (|r| < h), and all years up to the re-submission of a new bond.

Treatment timing / event date  
t = fiscal year immediately after election year; anticipation captured by k = −1 dummy in event study.

Running variable & cutoff  
r = Vote Share (%) – statutory threshold (66.67 % or 55 %).  
Cutoff at r = 0. Separate polynomials allowed pre/post-2001 or pool using threshold indicator.



--------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 3 ‑ KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. No precise manipulation of vote share around threshold  
 Plausible: individual votes are discrete; campaigns cannot target the exact last few votes. (McCrary density test feasible.)

A2. Potential outcomes evolve smoothly in r in absence of treatment  
 Plausible because the only discontinuous rule at r = 0 is legal passage of the bond.

A3. Local stable unit treatment value (no spillovers within h)  
 Plausible at district border level? Housing markets might spill; we later show robustness to excluding near-border transactions.

A4. Exclusion restriction for 2SLS: bond passage influences Y only through facility spending within the chosen window  
 Supported by legal earmarking; we also check that current spending, staffing, test administration, etc. do not jump at r = 0.

A5. Common support / overlap  
 Both sides of the cutoff are well-populated; 53 % of elections are within ±10 pp.



--------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 4 ‑ THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & REMEDIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Threat 1: Sorting/manipulation of turnout or mail-in ballots.  
 Remedy: (i) McCrary density test, (ii) placebo discontinuities at ±10 pp, (iii) covariate balance (pre-bond finance, enrollment).

Threat 2: Multiple bonds or “bunching” of elections.  
 Remedy: define event at first bond in a five-year window; drop districts that hold >1 election inside h within five years; robustness allowing later bonds but controlling for cumulative capital spending.

Threat 3: Concurrent statewide policy changes (e.g., accountability reforms 1999-2004).  
 Remedy: calendar-year fixed effects and interactions with district pre-bond characteristics; placebo RD at phantom thresholds of unrelated ballot props.



--------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 5 ‑ R CODE OUTLINE
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 0.  Libraries
# -------------------------------------------------------------
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)      # fast fixed-effect regressions
library(rdrobust)    # RDD inference
library(AER)         # ivreg

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load & merge data  (assume CSVs in ./data/)
# -------------------------------------------------------------
bonds   <- read_csv("./data/ca_bond_elections.csv")         # one row per election
finance <- read_csv("./data/ccd_district_finance.csv")      # district-year
houses  <- read_csv("./data/house_prices_blockgrp.csv")     # blockgrp-year
tests   <- read_csv("./data/test_scores_district.csv")

# District crosswalk & aggregation
houses_dist <- houses %>% 
  group_by(district_id, year) %>% 
  summarise(log_price = log(mean(price)), .groups="drop")

# Combine everything
panel <- finance %>% 
  left_join(houses_dist, by=c("district_id","year")) %>% 
  left_join(tests,        by=c("district_id","year")) %>% 
  left_join(bonds %>% 
              select(district_id, election_year, bond_amount, vote_share, threshold,
                     pass = passed),
            by = c("district_id" = "district_id", "year" = "election_year")) %>% 
  arrange(district_id, year) %>% 
  group_by(district_id) %>% 
  mutate(
    r   = vote_share - threshold,
    post = ifelse(!is.na(pass) & year > first(year[pass==1]),1,0),
    cap_spend_pp = capital_outlays / enrollment,
    treat       = post*pass
  ) %>% ungroup()

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. First-stage RDD check (rdrobust)
# -------------------------------------------------------------
rd_first <- rdrobust(y = panel$cap_spend_pp,
                     x = panel$r,
                     c = 0,
                     covs = model.matrix(~ enrollment + lag(enrollment), panel),
                     subset = abs(panel$r) <= 0.05)   # 5-pp window

summary(rd_first)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. 2SLS within bandwidth using fixest
# -------------------------------------------------------------
bw <- 0.05
sample <- panel %>% filter(abs(r) <= bw)

iv_spec <- feols(log_price ~ cap_spend_pp | pass,
                 data = sample,
                 fixef = ~ district_id + year,
                 cluster = "district_id")

summary(iv_spec)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Dynamic event study (robustness)
# -------------------------------------------------------------
event <- bonds %>% 
  mutate(event_id = row_number()) %>% 
  select(district_id, election_year, event_id)

panel2 <- panel %>% 
  left_join(event, by=c("district_id")) %>% 
  group_by(district_id) %>% 
  mutate(rel_year = year - election_year) %>% ungroup()

event_est <- feols(log_price ~ sunab(rel_year, pass) | district_id + year,
                   data = panel2 %>% filter(abs(r) <= bw),
                   cluster = "district_id")
iplot(event_est)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.  Placebo cut-off robustness
# -------------------------------------------------------------
placebo <- feols(log_price ~ pass + r | district_id + year,
                 data = panel %>% filter(r > 0.10 & r < 0.20),
                 cluster = "district_id")
summary(placebo)
```



--------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 6 ‑ EXPECTED RESULTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------
• Housing prices: Theory (Tiebout capitalization) predicts that $1 of present-value spending raises property values by ≤ $1 if households fully internalise costs; with California’s binding tax constraints, marginal capital may be high-value → expect elasticity > 1. Prior: a $10,000 increase in per-pupil capital stock (≈1 s.d.) raises log price by 2-3 %, equivalent to $1.20 of value per $1.

• Test scores: New/renovated facilities improve learning modestly; expect 0.03–0.07σ improvement in average 3rd/4th-grade math within five years, larger in lower-SES districts.

• Demographics: Slight increase in higher-income homebuyers; racial composition effects ambiguous.



--------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 7 ‑ VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (RDD)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: No manipulation at cutoff (McCrary) ........... 1  
C2: Covariate continuity within chosen bandwidth ... 1  
C3: Robust to alternative bandwidths/polynomials ... 1  
C4: Exclusion (only spending changes discontinuously) 0.5  
C5: Correct inference (clustered, robust, placebo) .. 1  

Total ≈ 4.5 / 5 – design appears credible but exclusion remains partly testable.



--------------------------------------------------------------------
